statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail risk is low at 16% while Stress remains high at 65%.
recommendation: Tail remains well below the 25% block threshold, so the deterministic mapping yields EA_ON. Elevated Stress reflects a 24-year high in the 30-year Treasury yield and the weakest consumer confidence since 2014 rather than an observed one-way Nasdaq-100 price path. A narrow danger window is published around the 12:30Z GDP and August PCE releases.
headline: Low Tail with high Stress: flat overnight NQ path ahead of August core PCE and annual GDP revisions
body: Nasdaq-100 futures are trading near 30,617, essentially unchanged overnight inside a narrow 0.46% range of 30,597.25 to 30,737.00, and have retraced roughly 120 points from the overnight high. The cash index closed the 29 September session at 30,339.33, up 0.21%, inside a 0.64% daily range and off its session lows, while the S&P 500 slipped 0.16% and the Dow fell 0.26%. VIX is 16.04. That combination of observed retracement, narrow ranges and low implied volatility is inconsistent with a pathological no-retracement path, so Tail stays low. Stress remains high for reasons that sit outside the Nasdaq-100 price path. The 30-year Treasury yield reached 5.62%, its highest since 2002, with the 10-year near 5.24% to 5.28% and the 2-year at 4.92%, a bear-steepening configuration that lifted mortgage rates to 7.58%. Conference Board consumer confidence fell 6.7 points to 81.9, the lowest since 2014, with the expectations component at 63.6 and consumers' view of business conditions negative for the first time since September 2024. August job openings were little changed at 7.1 million after a 256,000 decline. Against that softening demand picture, core inflation remains near 3.3%. Oil is elevated but easing, with WTI at 89.25 dollars and Brent at 96.09 dollars as Saudi pipeline repairs and a rebound in Middle East exports to 12.8 million barrels per day relieve supply pressure roughly seven months into the Iran conflict. Asian trade is mixed to firm, with the Nikkei up 1.4%, the Kospi up about 1%, the Hang Seng down 0.4% and the CSI 300 up 0.36%. The 1 October federal funding deadline is not a live discontinuity risk because a stopgap extending funding to 11 December has cleared both chambers. The principal forward catalyst is the 12:30Z block on 30 September: the third estimate of Q2 GDP and the August Personal Income and Outlays report, published alongside the BEA annual update to the national accounts, which can revise recent inflation history. Consensus places core PCE near 0.3% month over month and 3.3% to 3.4% year over year. Benchmark revisions widen the plausible reaction range and, with the long end already at a 24-year high, leave a credible conditional path for a bond-led delayed second leg into the cash open. Consistent with the contract, that unobserved scenario raises Stress and the published forecast Tail into the watch band around the release rather than the current Tail. Shared Finviz context was read but is 191 minutes old and partial, with the futures and calendar sections unavailable, so it was treated as stale supporting evidence only and not as current price-path evidence; its latest-session megacap dispersion, with Apple down 2.66% against Meta up 3.24%, is consistent with the rotational tape described above.

lookbackSummary: Over the past 24 hours the published Claude Tail score fell from the 23-24 watch band during the European morning of 29 September to 16 overnight, as the 29 September cash session closed off its lows and futures held an orderly range. Stress decayed steadily from 79 to 66 as the oil premium eased and the 1 October funding deadline was resolved by a stopgap, while remaining high throughout on long-end yield pressure. One hour, 14:00Z on 29 September, has no published assessment and is marked unavailable.
outlookSummary: The forecast holds Tail low through the Asian and European sessions on the observed two-sided overnight range, then lifts it into the 23-24 watch band across 12:00Z to 14:00Z for the GDP third estimate, the August PCE report and the accompanying BEA annual revisions, with the 13:30Z cash open and 13:45Z Chicago PMI inside that window. Tail eases back below the watch threshold through the US afternoon on assumed volatility decay, edges up again for the 19:00Z closing hour on quarter-end imbalance flows, and settles at 17-18 overnight into 1 October. Stress peaks near 76 around the release and declines to the mid-60s by the Asian open. Confidence declines from 87 to 79 across the horizon as the verified evidence sample ages. Every hour beyond the current clock-hour is conditional.
